messages.task:
You are a financial analysis assistant.  You have access to a set of callable tools that expose structured data and basic math utilities.  Use these tools to reason step-by-step and produce a concise final answer to the user’s question.

Scenario description (background information the company disclosed – no need to quote back):
During the year ended December 31, 2011, the company granted 354,660 performance share units (PSUs) with a fair value based on the grant-date closing stock price of $28.79.  For legacy Frontier PSUs assumed on July 1 2011, performance is tied to total shareholder return relative to a peer group and payouts can range from 0-125 % of target.  These legacy PSUs were valued on July 1 2011 with a Monte-Carlo model, resulting in a fair value of $8.6 million.  Of this amount, $7.3 million relates to post-merger services and will be recognized ratably through 2013.

Available tools (Python callables you may invoke):
• list_all_grants() – return metadata for every equity grant in the database.
• find_grant_ids_by_date(date_iso) – get grant_id(s) that match a specific grant date like "2011-07-01".
• find_grant_ids_by_keyword(keyword) – search grant descriptions; returns matching grant_id(s).
• get_grant_fair_value_million(grant_id) – fetch the total fair value (millions USD) for a grant.
• list_components_for_grant(grant_id) – list each component name and amount (millions) for that grant.
• get_component_amount_million(grant_id, component_name) – retrieve a single component’s amount.
• difference(minuend, subtrahend) – simple subtraction utility.
• percentage(numerator, denominator) – compute (numerator / denominator) × 100.
• average_fair_value_of_noise_grants(before_year=2012) – returns an average for unrelated grants (not required for this task).

Question to answer:
What percentage of the July 2011 performance share value does NOT relate to post-merger services?

Instructions: Think through which tools will give you the information you need, call them, do the math, and reply with the final percentage formatted like "12.3%" (one decimal point, percent sign).
